Schwedt-Oder (port locode DESDT) is an Oder River cruise port and town in Germany's Brandenburg state (Uckermark district) with population around 30,000. The town is located close to the Germany-Poland border. Uckermark is a historic region stretching between two rivers (Oder and Havel) and running along the state border. Across the Oder River (approx 10 km / 6 mi to the southeast) is Chojna Poland (fka Konigsberg in der Neumark). The nearest German towns are Angermunde (18 km / 11 mi to the west) and Gartz (18 km down the river).

At the end of WW2 (1939-1945), most of the town (over 85%) was destroyed during the 2-month heavy fighting.

The Oder River originates in the Czech Republic and flows approx 740 km (460 mi) through Poland. For 187 km (116 mi), the river forms part of the Oder-Neisse line (Germany-Poland border). The Oder flows into the Szczecin Lagoon (north of Szczecin Poland) and then into three river branches (Dziwna, Swina, Peene) that empty into the Baltic Sea via Bay of Pomerania.

As a cruise port, Schwedt-Oder was included in the 2019 schedules of the riverboats Saxonia (2001-built) and Katharina von Bora (2000-built).
